answer: Topological bridge scarcity counts how many independent paths connect a node to the rest of the mesh. Each new identity must attach through at least three disjoint routes, so an attacker pays for real link capacity at every bridge, not just a cheap endpoint. A cluster that routes through one shared knoll gets flagged because its internal fan-out collapses under path sampling, forcing duplicate identities onto costly redundant links. Any operator wanting a haven of many fake nodes must fund genuine multi-hop connectivity per identity, which scales cost linearly with count.
